e-4350.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,-4,2 \rangle,$ $\mathbf{b}=\langle 0,-2,1 \rangle,$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -1,0,3 \rangle.$
e-4350.worked_solution:
The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|-(-4)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2\cdot 3-1\cdot 0)+4(0\cdot 3-1\cdot (-1))+2(0\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot (-2)) \\  & =-6+4-4 \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the absolute value. So the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is

$$
V = |-6| = 6.
$$

e-4351.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle k,2,1 \rangle,$ $\mathbf{b}=\langle -2,-1,1 \rangle,$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -1,1,2 \rangle$ are coplanar.
e-4351.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(-1\cdot 2-1\cdot 1)-2(-2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1)+(-2\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-3k+6-3 \\  & =-3k+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ -3k+3 & =0 \\ k & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=1$.

e-4352.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(3,-1,2),$ $B(2,1,1),$ $C(-1,2,1),$ and $D(4,4,2).$
e-4352.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-i+2j-k \\  & =⟨-1,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+2j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-4i+3j-k \\  & =⟨-4,3,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(4i+4j+2k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =i+5j \\  & =⟨1,5,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3\cdot 0-5\cdot (-1))-2((-4)\cdot 0-1\cdot (-1))-((-4)\cdot 5-1\cdot 3) \\  & =-5-2+23 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is

$$
V=|16|=16.
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,1,4⟩,$ $b=⟨8,0,3⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,1⟩$ are coplanar.
after.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 1 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+4\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(0\cdot 1-1\cdot 3)-(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 3)+4(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 0) \\  & =-3k+1+32 \\  & =33-3k \\  & =3(11-k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 3(11-k) & =0 \\ 11-k & =0 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

after.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 6 \\ t & t & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & 2 \\ 2 & 7\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & 2 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}|+6\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & t \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-3(t\cdot 7-(-1)\cdot 2)+6(t\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot t) \\  & =-21t-6+12t+6t \\  & =-3t-6.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ -3t-6 & =0 \\ -3t & =6 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=-2.$

after.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 7 \\ t & 4 & t \\ 2 & 6 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & t \\ 6 & 8\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & t \\ 2 & 8\end{aligned}|+7\cdot |\begin{aligned}t & 4 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(4\cdot 8-6\cdot t)+(t\cdot 8-2\cdot t)+7(t\cdot 6-2\cdot 4) \\  & =96-18t+8t-2t+42t-56 \\  & =30t+40 \\  & =10(3t+4).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 10(3t+4) & =0 \\ 3t+4 & =0 \\ t & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=-\frac{4}{3}.$

First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-2i+2j+3k)-(i-j+2k) \\  & =-3i+3j+k \\  & =⟨-3,3,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i+j+k)-(i-j+2k) \\  & =2j-k \\  & =⟨0,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(-i+3j-2k)-(i-j+2k) \\  & =-2i+4j-4k \\  & =⟨-2,4,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -4\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(2\cdot (-4)-4\cdot (-1))-3(0\cdot (-4)-(-2)\cdot (-1))+(0\cdot 4-(-2)\cdot 2) \\  & =12+6+4 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|22|=22.
$$
